feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/editorial blend is compelling. It reads polished and modern, though it would be stronger with tighter consolidation, more outcome-focused metrics, and a few consistency fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility in digital platforms, governance, and communications.  
- Good evidence of scale and impact: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and analytics stack details add substance.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned to the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and more space for achievements.  
- Add sharper results language: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes; include measurable improvements where possible (engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance).  
- Fix style consistency: use one name format (“Coleman Davis,” not “DAVIS”); standardize punctuation around lists and hyphenation (e.g., “organization-wide,” “member-facing”). No major misspellings or grammar errors found, but there are minor stylistic inconsistencies in bullet formatting and emphasis.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly dense and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a tighter lead.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct phrasing like “leading digital platforms, governance, and content operations for” to improve clarity.
- Add scale or audience context from recent roles, e.g. “enterprise web platforms serving millions of annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing the list length.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives enterprise website modernization, analytics and editorial infrastructure, and multimedia and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it broad here and let later sections provide detail.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems” closely echoes Core Competencies.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use sharper, more parallel phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search work.
- Change “operations” to “leadership” where appropriate to better reflect director/consultant seniority.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “governance & editorial systems” vs. “multimedia production and livestream operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making it shorter or more executive-level.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets and may be redundant unless it is a target-role keyword.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked nouns.
- Where possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale indicator instead of only listing features.
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current NACo bullets; this footer should emphasize standout outcomes, formats, or technologies not already stated.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it or expanding it slightly while trimming repeated web/platform language.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical breadth, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with both the prior NACo roles and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, scope, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, campaign delivery, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery across member-facing digital platforms.”
- Replace task-heavy bullets with 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; e.g. “Built Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsite templates, and downloadable toolkits to support member engagement and advocacy campaigns.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance language: “Improved cross-channel workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia operations.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages/templates launched, teams supported, workflow time reduced, search/discovery improvements, or campaign performance gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects rail; keep one concise mention here and let the project section carry detail.
- Web governance/analytics/workflows strongly overlaps with Director of Digital Media; emphasize advisory/consulting scope and new initiatives instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one sharper achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight outcome-focused: add growth, engagement, production volume, or efficiency metrics for email/social/video if available; otherwise keep this bullet shorter.
- Rephrase ops/analytics bullets to show business impact: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership visibility and decision-making” and “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current email/newsletter and recurring video language overlaps with the 2018–2022 role.
- “Governance” and “analytics infrastructure” already appear in the header/skills, so keep this item achievement-led.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows how this role built the foundation for the later director position.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Video program language also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and footer project list.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most marketable differentiators.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Web governance and modernization strategy” if targeting digital platform leadership roles; it aligns better with recent experience.
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership traits with execution tasks.
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the section title or nearby summary instead of here (e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ publisher environments”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat almost verbatim from Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than achievements already shown in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Use broader, senior phrasing like “enterprise CMS delivery” or “platform implementation” to match Director/consulting-level experience.
- If space allows, align to proven impact themes from recent roles: “Drupal modernization for high-volume public sites” or “search and workflow systems for multi-publisher teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” is already repeated in Technical + IT; avoid duplicating the same list verbatim.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in only one place or varying the phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and business impact over platform names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcome-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI frameworks and executive reporting” before listing platforms.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider revised line: “- Analytics strategy and KPI design - Executive dashboards and decision support - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating every tool here if they are already listed in Technical + IT; use this section to signal senior-level capability instead.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, current capabilities and make it feel more senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace generic list with a tighter, senior-focused set:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and studio system operations
- Virtual event delivery and technical troubleshooting
- If accurate, consider adding scale/complexity language: “broadcast-quality,” “recurring advocacy programming,” or “in-house studio production” to align with recent leadership roles.
- Keep to 4 bullets max; remove filler like “video production and editing” if stronger phrasing is available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates Core Competencies: “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close enough that they can be consolidated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is clearly the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, the item should reflect that hierarchy.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by demonstrated depth and recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency framing to show emphasis, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more outcome-linked: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites; modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid mixing “CMS” and broader site-hosting tools without context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one or using this section for only named tools while the topline section emphasizes capabilities.
- GitHub Pages is the least supported by experience; remove it if space is tight or evidence is limited.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical breadth, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and separate coding from platform skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows**
- Drop version numbers unless required; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built custom Drupal front-end components,” “deployed serverless scripts via Cloudflare Workers,” or “automated deployment/testing with GitHub Actions.”
- Consider replacing older/less strategic items with stronger recent tools if used more often (e.g., TypeScript, REST/JSON, CI/CD, performance optimization).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; keep it in one place or vary this section to focus on implementation tooling.
- “API integrations” and “workflow automation” also overlap with other skills sections.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and group by function: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project operations)”
- Consider replacing one or two lower-value collaboration tools with stronger systems evidence if accurate, e.g., “Forms/approvals,” “cross-platform automations,” or “editorial workflow design”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless central to operations; they may dilute stronger automation tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Because the CV already shows strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform breadth and enterprise-level use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email marketing, member communications, journey automation)**
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of just names: **Enterprise email and engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp**
- Keep the newest/most strategic platform first; if Dynamics is your strongest recent tool, leave the order as-is.
- Only include platforms you used directly in administration, buildout, segmentation, automation, or reporting—not just as an end user.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “audiences,” or “multi-channel communications” here; those are already covered in recent work experience and core competencies.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider naming it in a work bullet instead of expanding this skills line too much.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” As a technical list, it should be tighter, more tool-focused, and avoid generic capability terms unless they add distinct value.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with a specific platform or remove it; dashboarding is an output, not a tool.
- Consider replacing broad **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis** for better specificity.
- Order by strategic weight/recent relevance: analytics stack first, then behavior/optimization tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep this version strictly technical and leave KPI/reporting language in Topline Skills.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so this section should stay concise rather than restating impact.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since leadership, governance, and scaled operations are already covered in newer entries.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia production.”
- Add clearer scope/results if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or videos produced, email volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital production workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger verb if accurate: “mentored,” “supervised,” or “trained” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 roles; keep this version focused on foundational setup, not governance.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the next role; distinguish this one as launching or initially producing the series.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with one clear differentiator—the first podcast launch—but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize initiative, cross-functional coordination, and any concrete output.

Suggested edit
- Recast around the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy-support projects for NACo programs, while expanding digital storytelling through multimedia content and the launch of the organization’s first podcast.”
- Add ownership and scope: “Led podcast planning, scripting, guest/stakeholder coordination, and production from concept to launch.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced multimedia and digital content supporting program communications and policy initiatives.”
- If possible, add a measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal teams supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered in later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on innovation/project coordination + first podcast launch.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since stronger management evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so keep this entry software/tool-focused.
